key_insight: GREx generalizes referring-expression tasks by supporting multi-target and no-target expressions across segmentation, comprehension, and generation, filling a major gap in existing datasets and methods.
problem_solved: Existing REx (RES/REC/REG) benchmarks and models assume single-target expressions only; this work addresses realism and scalability by enabling and evaluating multi-target and no-target referring expressions.
method: Introduce a set of new datasets/benchmarks that include multi-target and no-target referring expressions for unified evaluation across RES, REC, and REG.

Propose a unified framework (GREx) that handles segmentation, detection, and generation tasks under the generalized referring-expression setting with shared representations and cross-task supervision.
Design an evaluation protocol and metrics tailored to multi-target and no-target scenarios, and provide baseline models and analyses to quantify gains and failure modes.
impact: GREx makes referring-expression research more applicable to real-world vision–language systems by broadening task scope and evaluation, enabling models that handle complex, ambiguous, or absent references. Practitioners can use the datasets and protocols to build and benchmark more robust multimodal agents.

paper_title: GREx: Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation, Comprehension, and Generation
paper_authors: Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, Shuting He, Xudong Jiang, Yu-Gang Jiang
